turns.q: Tell me about yourself?
turns.answer:
I'm Jon — an independent web designer based in Bordeaux[[bordeaux]], though I'm originally from Jersey[[jersey]] and lived in Paris and Brighton along the way. I've been designing and building for the web for over 25 years, working across strategy, design and development, which is a rare mix for one person.

Outside work I'm a keen street photographer, shooting with a Leica, and I usually have music on whilst I work or cook. I'm drawn to places with a bit of a bad reputation — I love to travel.

turns.q: Do you like Japan?
turns.answer:
I loved Japan. I spent a few weeks there towards the end of a big trip, and it completely got under my skin — the food, the visual culture, and this odd, warm sense of connection with people even when we barely shared a language. It's one of the few places I actively wanted to go back to.

[[next: what were you doing in Japan? @note:lost-in-conversation-kyoto | did you take many photos there? @photo:street-photo | how did a year of travelling shape your work? @about]]

turns.q: Do you like Japan?
turns.answer:
I loved it — I spent about three weeks there once, coming up from South East Asia, and it completely rewired how I travel. What struck me was how much I enjoyed staying put longer, getting to know a few people and places properly rather than rushing through sights.

I ended up spending time with a collective of architects in Kyoto, which was genuinely inspiring — seeing how they lived and worked together. The design, the food, the little cultural surprises: it's a place that rewards paying attention.

[[next: what were the architects in Kyoto like? @note:geneto-architects-kyoto-and-tokyo | what kind of photography did you shoot while travelling? @photo:street-photo | how did that year of travelling shape your work? @about]]

turns.q: Do you like Japan?
turns.answer:
I loved Japan. turns.q: Tell me about the White Paper project
turns.answer:
White Paper are a long-standing client — the UK's leading provider of legal and business CPD conferences, going 20 years. I rebuilt their booking engine and on-demand platform from the ground up, taking a clunky eight-step booking flow and consolidating a mess of disconnected systems into one.

[[casestudies:white-paper-booking-engine-design-development]]

The results were the part I'm proudest of — big drops in checkout abandonment and processing time, and on-demand now pulls in a healthy chunk of their revenue.

turns.q: What did you do for White Paper?
turns.answer:
I designed and rebuilt their booking engine and on-demand platform — they're the UK's leading provider of legal and business CPD conferences, and it's a relationship I'm still in. The old booking journey was long and leaky, so I rethought the whole thing and consolidated years of scattered conference data into one place.

[[casestudies]]

[[next: how did you cut the booking drop-off? @study:white-paper-booking-engine-design-development | what does the on-demand platform do? @study:white-paper-booking-engine-design-development | how do you usually approach a project like this? @method]]

turns.q: What results did the booking engine deliver?
turns.answer:
The big ones: drop-off fell by around 90%, the number of steps to book came down by 50–60%, and back-office processing time dropped by about 85% — enough that they went from four people handling bookings to one. On-demand also grew into roughly a third of their revenue.
